DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) infection.

The clinical presentation of a generalized rash with potential vesicular or pustular changes, combined with systemic symptoms like lethargy and poor feeding, is highly suggestive of a neonatal HSV infection. The Gram stain, Tzanck test, and clinical images will be critical for confirmation; I await the results of the blood cultures and CBC to rule out bacterial sepsis as a differential.
